policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's conditional wording 'if Absalom had lived' distinguishes the qere לוּ ('if') from the ketiv לא ('not').
ASV 'what he thought good' permits both בעיניו and בעינו; the two notes are alternative_rendering notes and therefore do not decide the textual reading.
ASV 'to conduct him over the Jordan' renders the qere הַיַּרְדֵּן as the object of crossing and distinguishes it from ketiv בירדן ('in/by the Jordan').
ASV 'all the people of Judah brought the king over' uses the causative sense of qere הֶעֱבִירוּ, distinguishing it from ketiv ויעברו ('and they went over').
